fi-dermogenys-pusilla.title: Platinum Wrestling Halfbeak
fi-dermogenys-pusilla.summary: The wrestling halfbeak, Dermogenys pusilla, is a halfbeak widespread from India and Myanmar east to Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia. Males fight by locking jaws, and in some of its native…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Widespread in nature, it is known from India, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia and Indonesia.
notes: Surface area is more important than depth with this species, as it spends almost all of its time just under the water surface.
It's a particularly flighty species, particularly when first introduced to a new tank.

fi-nandus-nandus.title: Nandus Asian Leaf Fish
fi-nandus-nandus.summary: Nandus nandus, commonly known as the Gangetic leaffish, is a species of Asian leaffish native to South Asia and Indochina. They are common in slow-moving or stagnant bodies of water, including…
rows: Up to about 20.0 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-toxotes-jaculatrix.title: Banded Archerfish
fi-toxotes-jaculatrix.summary: The classic archerfish, famous for spitting jets of water to knock insects off overhanging leaves. A brackish-water fish from mangroves and estuaries that gets fairly large.
rows: Generally peaceful, but eats much smaller fish and can bicker with its own kind
Groups of 4–5 or more spread squabbling (OATA suggests 6+)
Insect eater. Wild fish take land and water invertebrates and the odd small fish; in tanks it takes floating pellets and flake plus frozen foods
Brackish; archerfish do well at low-to-medium brackish levels
India and Southeast Asia to the western Pacific islands and northern Australia; mangroves and estuaries
notes: A tall tank only half filled, with plants above the waterline, lets it hunt by spitting at crickets or fruit flies placed on the leaves.
Keep the water flow slow; mangrove roots and brackish-tolerant plants suit it.

fi-monodactylus-argenteus.title: Mono (Silver Moony)
fi-monodactylus-argenteus.summary: A bright silver, diamond-shaped schooling fish with yellow-edged fins. Young monos live in brackish estuaries; adults move toward full seawater, so plan for salt as it grows.
rows: Up to about 10.5 in (27 cm SL); commonly around 5 in
Keep a group of at least six
Omnivore; in the wild it feeds on plankton and detritus
Brackish while young; adults do best in full-strength seawater
Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Samoa and Australia; bays, mangrove estuaries and lower rivers
notes: Mostly juveniles enter fresh water in the wild; raise salinity gradually as it matures.

fi-selenotoca-multifasciata.title: Silver Scat
fi-selenotoca-multifasciata.summary: A deep-bodied, silvery scat with thin dark bars and spots, from estuaries and mangrove creeks of Indonesia and Australia. A large, social brackish-to-marine fish.
rows: Up to about 16 in (40 cm SL)
Keep a group of at least six
Brackish while young; adults do best in full-strength seawater
Sulawesi and Indonesia to western and eastern Australia and New Caledonia; estuaries, river mouths and mangrove creeks
warn: Venomous fin spines: net and handle carefully.

sources.name: OATA care sheet – monos, scats & archerfish

fi-nomorhamphus-liemi.title: Celebes Halfbeak
fi-nomorhamphus-liemi.summary: A livebearing halfbeak from the highland streams of southern Sulawesi (Celebes). It likes cooler water and some current, and eats mostly insects.
rows: Ignores most tankmates, but males fight each other and small fish get eaten
Mainly insects: live insects such as fruit flies and crickets are an important part of its diet
notes: Livebearer: young are born large (up to about 1 in) every 4–6 weeks, and mothers hunt them.
